## The trap (burned ~2h on 2026-07-03)

You land routine-behavior code in the staging tree (new fields on a loop fire, a new
wake payload, changed scheduling logic). Tests are green, the feature flag is ON, the
routine row in PG is correct — and yet **the live behavior never changes, with zero
errors anywhere**.

Concrete incident: the cold-auto loop producer (`su-cold-auto-mode-2026-07-03`).
`loop:arm { carry:'cold' }` was accepted, the carry-note anchor existed, the
`papercusp-su-cold-auto` flag was ON, the routine's `payload_template` carried
`carry:'cold'` — and **every single loop fire still went out WARM** (delivery rows had
`payload NULL`, channel `psu-socket-inject`). Two live test agents (su-54eef, su-4777)
reported 13 consecutive warm wakes.

## Root cause

**All durable routine fires execute on `papercup-bg-host.service`** — the dedicated
background host ("DBOS routines / git-sync / substrate primary"). Its DBOS
`routinesTick` claims every due routine, so *it* runs `fireLoopWake` etc., not the
`:3070` operator you probably restarted/deployed.

The bg-host `tsx`-loads the **staging working tree once, at process start**, and
restarts only on failure (memory-watchdog / freeze-watchdog / `Restart=always`). So it
keeps executing its boot-time code snapshot indefinitely. In the incident it had been
up since 07:37; the cold-marker code landed 08:46; every fire it claimed used the old
`fireLoopWake` and stamped no cold payload.

DBOS attribution made this provable: `dbos.workflow_status` rows for `routineFire`
showed `executor_id = bg-host-3270` on all 11 fires.

## How to see it / fix it

- **`dev:service_health`** now reports a **`bg-host-code`** probe (WI-1867): it compares
  the bg-host process start against the newest on-disk `*.ts` mtime under the routine
  hot paths (`operator-core/lib/dbos`, `lib/harness/routines`, `lib/events`,
  `lib/agent-tools/loop`) and flags `⚠ bg-host CODE DRIFT` when the code on disk is
  younger than the process. Drift is a warning (`up:true`) — it never fires a
  down-transition or auto-restart.
- Fix = `systemctl --user restart papercup-bg-host.service`. It is `Restart=always`
  and DBOS work is durable, but **a restart reclaims in-flight cup spawns**
  (EI-2186/EI-2434) — restart deliberately, not on a timer, and prefer a quiet moment.
- Rule of thumb: **if your change touches how routines/loops/wakes FIRE, restarting
  `:3070` (or `:3170`) is not enough — the bg-host is the host that runs it.**

## Corollary: the DELIVERING host matters too — the pump is a SKIP LOCKED race

Fixing the *emitting* host is not the whole story. A wake delivery row is claimed
SKIP LOCKED by **whichever process pumps first** — the emitter's in-process
`setImmediate` kick (engine.ts `emitAwaitedEvent`) *usually* wins, but the periodic
sweep on ANY other live operator host can steal it. **Each wake then executes the code
vintage of its claiming host**, so behavior is nondeterministic across a deploy skew.

Concrete continuation of the same incident (2026-07-03, root cause #3 of three): after
the bg-host was restarted onto fixed code, delivery **#4963 still went WARM** — the
`papercup-dev-api` (`:3070`, release checkout on `main`, which lacked the fix) journal
had the `[await-event] wake #4963 delivered … via psu-socket-inject` line. Minutes
later delivery **#4972 went COLD** (`psu-socket-reset`) — pumped 1.2s after fire by the
bg-host kick. Same routine, same payload, opposite outcomes — decided purely by which
host won the claim.

Implications:

- A wake-behavior fix is only **deterministically** live once it reaches EVERY host
  that can pump: the bg-host (restart it) AND `:3070` (reaches it only via the
  green-checkpoint → deploy pipeline — `dev:pipeline_position <sha>` tells you where
  your commit is). Until then expect *intermittent* old behavior, not consistent
  failure.
- Attribution: grep ALL candidate journals for the delivery id
  (`journalctl --user -u papercup-{bg-host,dev-api,staging-api}.service | grep 'wake #<id>'`)
  — the `dbos.workflow_status` executor only names the EMITTING host.

## Diagnosing "my loop wake behaved wrong" in general

1. `harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries` — the fire's row: `source` = `loop:<routineId>`
   for a real loop fire (vs `coord:inbox-wake` message wakes — an agent cannot tell
   them apart from the inside!), `payload` = the marker the fire stamped, `channel` =
   what the wake-executor did (`psu-socket-inject` warm / `psu-socket-reset` /
   `psu-socket-recycle` cold).
2. `dbos.workflow_status WHERE name='routineFire'` — `executor_id` tells you WHICH host
   ran the fire; check that host's age vs your code.
3. Grep the service journals for `wake #<delivery-id>` to find which host PUMPED the
   delivery (the SKIP LOCKED race above) — the fire host and the pump host can differ.
4. Only then read the code — it may be correct and simply not loaded (or loaded on one
   host and not the other).
